To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the satisfiability problem for XPath fragments with and/or without negation is PTIME-complete for acyclic DTDs, EXPTIME-complete for DTDs without recursion or data-value joins, and NEXPTIME-complete when recursion and data-value tests are present.
(i) the satisfiability problem is NP-hard in the presence of data values; (ii) in the absence of data values it is PSPACE-complete in the presence of negation, and

the satisfiability problem for XPath fragments without data values and negations is NP-complete, and for fragments with negations and without data values it is PSPACE-complete, and in the presence both of data values and of negations it is EXPTIME-complete.

the impact of DTDs on the complexity of XPath satisfiability, and the results are of practical relevance to the development of XML query optimizers and validators.
